Name: Antibodies.com
Description:
Antibodies.com supplies high-quality antibodies, ELISA kits, proteins, assay kits, and other companion products to life science researchers. Our mission is to help advance biology research and drug discovery by enabling researchers to discover more, for less. 

Headquartered in Cambridge (UK), and with offices in Stockholm (SE) and St Louis (MO, USA), we can support your research with high-quality and characterized research tools, expert customer service, detailed product datasheets, and fast global delivery. Our growing product range caters for every discipline and includes: primary antibodies, secondary antibodies, ELISA kits, cell based assays, recombinant proteins, aptamers, IVD raw materials and other companion products.

Name: Akrivia Health
Description:
Akrivia Health was founded to answer a critical question: Why is mental health and dementias research still decades behind?

Spun out of the NHS and Oxford University in 2019, we’re focused on curating the world’s most in-depth neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative dataset – linking structured and unstructured EHRs with genomic and longitudinal insights. 
Because what is urgently needed in this space is faster access to better quality data.

Our AI-enabled solutions apply advanced NLP to extract deep phenotypic signals from clinical notes, enabling patient stratification, outcome tracking, and real-world evidence generation.

Through this, we enable researchers, pharma, and healthcare providers to evaluate treatment effectiveness, optimise clinical trials, and drive precision care.

Join us to transform the future of mental health and dementias and improve lives – one data point at a time.

Name: TGI Life Sciences
Description:
TGI Life Sciences is a highly effective recruitment partner that offers their clients more than just a service provider. We achieve this with highly experienced consultants that seek to understand each and every client's growth and development goals.

At Biofidelity, we’re working toward a future where more people around the world have access to the life-changing power of genomics. Our novel molecular technologies simplify genomic analysis, so more patients have access to the information needed to ensure the best possible outcomes. 

Our vision doesn’t end with oncology, though. Our revolutionary technologies will pave the way for tomorrow’s yet-unknown scientific breakthroughs.

Name: Benchmark Holdings plc
Description:

Name: Baseimmune
Description: Baseimmune was founded in 2019 as a discovery phase start-up in the antigen discovery and vaccine development field.

Name: Crescendo Biologics Limited
Description:
Crescendo Biologics is a private, clinical stage immuno-oncology company developing novel, targeted T cell enhancing Humabody therapeutics.

Leading its proprietary pipeline, Crescendo Biologics has developed CB307, a novel half-life extended CD137 x PSMA Humabody for the selective activation of tumour-specific T cells exclusively within the tumour microenvironment. CB307 is designed to achieve a longer lasting anti-cancer effect whilst avoiding systemic toxicity, and the clinical programme for CB307 is underway in patients with PSMA positive solid tumours (NCT04839991). CB693 is a half-life extended CD137 x MSLN Humabody and is the second proprietary clinical candidate from Crescendo’s T cell enhancing pipeline. Crescendo is also developing CB213, a preclinical PD-1 x LAG-3 multi-specific Humabody.

The Company’s ability to develop multi-functional Humabody therapeutics is based on its unique, patent protected, transgenic mouse platform generating fully human VH domain building blocks (Humabody VH). These robust molecules can be configured to engage therapeutic targets in such a way that they deliver novel pharmacology and superior bio-distribution. This can lead to larger therapeutic windows compared to conventional IgG approaches. Humabody-based formats can also be applied across a range of non-cancer indications. 

Beyond Crescendo’s proprietary pipeline, the Company has global, multi-target discovery and development collaborations with both Takeda and BioNTech and an exclusive, worldwide licensing agreement with Zai Lab for ZL-1102 (formerly CB001, an anti-IL-17A targeting Humabody), which is expected to enter global Phase 2 clinical development in patients with psoriasis. 

Crescendo Biologics is located in Cambridge, UK, and is backed by blue-chip investors including Sofinnova Partners, Andera Partners, IP Group, BioNTech, Takeda and Quan Capital. For more information, please visit www.crescendobiologics.com.

Name: Innovation Forum

The Innovation Forum is an international grassroots network that supports scientific entrepreneurs aiming to build ambitious companies at the intersection of science, technology and health.

Description:
Globally Trusted Screening Solutions

Randox Food Diagnostics offer excellent tools for screening for mycotoxins,  antimicrobials, growth promoting hormones and drugs of abuse in animals and produce. Name: Phytoform

Name: Draig Therapeutics
Description:
Draig Therapeutics is a clinical-stage company with a mission to transform treatments in Neuropsychiatry. The company is leveraging its founders’ unique scientific expertise in modulating the core glutamate / GABA pathways that play a critical role in neuropsychiatric diseases to advance a pipeline of groundbreaking therapies designed to address large unmet patient needs, including in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD).

Draig is the Welsh word for ‘dragon’ and it reflects the company’s origins in Wales. The name and logo were inspired by this heritage, reflecting its scientific roots stemming from Cardiff University.

Fluidic Analytics designs, develops and manufactures tools that seek to revolutionise the way proteins are characterised, allowing our customers to understand the machinery of life.

We envision a world where information about proteins and their behaviour transforms our understanding of how the biological world operates, and helps all of us make better decisions about how we diagnose diseases, develop treatments and maintain our personal well-being.

By building the world’s best tools, software and services for protein characterisation and making them universally accessible in the lab, in the clinic or at home, we are making this vision a reality not just for a small group of expert users, but for everyone who can benefit.

Twitter: @fluidicanalytic

Name: CooperGenomics

Description: Amici provides a purchasing and supply chain management service, allowing biotech organisations to focus on discovering life changing innovations. Our experts will save you time and money while our easy-to-use software will give you the traceability and control that you need.

Name: Sitryx
Description:
Sitryx is a biopharmaceutical company focused on regulating cell metabolism to develop first-in-class disease modifying therapeutics in immuno-oncology and immuno-inflammation.

The company was co-founded by a team of world-leading scientists from the United States and Europe who have contributed significantly to the field of immunometabolism. 

Sitryx was founded in 2018 with seed funding from SV Health Investors and raised $30 million Series A funding from an international syndicate of specialist investors including SV Health Investors, Sofinnova Partners, Longwood Fund and GSK. The company has a pipeline of projects at multiple stages of drug discovery. Sitryx is headquartered in Oxford, UK.

Name: Dolomite Microfluidics
Description:
Dolomite is the world leader in design and manufacture of high quality innovative microfluidic products.

We offer a broad range of modular microfluidic systems, modules and components such as pumps, chips, connectors, temperature controllers, sensors, accessories and software for analysis or automation. We also regularly design and manufacture custom-made components or modules to exactly match a customer’s requirement and perform product design & development for complete instruments.

Dolomite’s systems and products are used in a wide range of applications, including:

- Biology e.g. cell encapsulation in microdroplets and analysis of individual cells from a population
- Drug discovery e.g. drug formulation and controlled release via biodegradable particles
- Chemistry e.g. nano & microparticle synthesis and petrochemical analysis
- Food and cosmetics e.g. bulk precision manufacturing of emulsions and foams
- Academia e.g. study of microfluidics and microfluidic droplets or bubbles

Based in Royston (near Cambridge), UK, Dolomite is part of Unchained Labs. We have offices in the USA, Japan, UK & China and worldwide distributors offering technical assistance and support. Dolomite excels in commercialising microfluidic products which exceed expectations.

Name: Peptone
Description: Peptone is a therapeutics company that uses AI and an experimental physics product engine to design small molecules targeting the 6,200 intrinsically disordered human proteins that Alpha Fold 3 cannot model.

Name: AlphaBiolabs
Description:
At AlphaBiolabs, we help family law professionals, social workers and local authorities obtain the reliable, court-approved evidence they need to make critical safeguarding decisions.
 
As the UK's No.1 UKAS 17025-accredited laboratory, we provide court-approved Drug, Alcohol and DNA testing across the UK and Ireland. Our results are accepted by Family Courts, the Ministry of Justice, Home Office, HM Passport Office, and UKVI.
 
Unlike some labs, all testing is carried out in our UK laboratory.
 
We offer a comprehensive range of court-approved testing services, including drug and alcohol testing using hair, nail, blood, oral fluid, and urine samples, as well as breath alcohol testing and SCRAM CAM. We also deliver industry-leading DNA relationship testing for child welfare, custody, and immigration cases, testing for all family relationships including paternity, non-invasive prenatal paternity (NIPP) and extended family testing.  
 
Every case is managed by a dedicated Case Manager who oversees the process from instruction to delivery. 
 
Our nationwide network of professional clinicians can collect samples from any location. We also offer FREE legally-instructed sample collections from any of our 21 walk-in centres across the UK and Ireland – a proposition unique to AlphaBiolabs – so testing can be arranged quickly, wherever your client is located.
 
All pricing is within Legal Aid Agency rates and our Price Promise guarantees that we will beat any like-for-like quote by a further 10%.
 
To request a quote or discuss a case, contact our New Enquiry team on 0333 600 1300, email testing@alphabiolabs.com, or complete our online quote form https://www.alphabiolabs.co.uk/legal-test-forms/.

Name: Bionema Group Limited
Description:
Bionema Group - ABOUT US:

Are you deeply concerned about the harmful effects of chemical pesticides on human health and the environment?

Look no further than Bionema, a TRAILBLAZER in biocontrol technology with over 30 years of experience pioneering research, Bionema stands as a leader in offering sustainable, natural pests, disease, and plant health management solutions that directly address this critical issue linked to food security.

Special biofertilizers and biostimulants are crucial for efficient plant growth. Combining cutting-edge research, we provide these vital tools to our farmers, growers, greenkeepers, and foresters.

Customer satisfaction and quality are our core values. We tailor technology to meet the individual needs.

Our product categories include but are not limited:

•	Liquid, WP, Encapsulated formulation of biostimulants and biofertilisers for plant health management.

#biocontroltechnology #sustainablefarmingsolutions,

Name: Phenomic
Description:
Phenomic’s mission is to raise the survival curve for the hardest to treat solid tumors (e.g., colorectal, pancreatic, breast cancers). We believe the reason why drugs for these cancers have not translated well in the clinic historically is that they were largely discovered and studied in models that do not account for the diversity of cell types present in human tumors. To address this challenge, we have built an ML-powered transcriptomics platform that allows us to understand the interactions of all the cell types in these tumors to identify compelling targets and a system to test our drugs in human tumor explants thus delivering translational insights during our discovery process.

Our lead program is a CD3 engager that uses a novel targeting approach identified by our platform that should be able to overcome limitations of traditional tumor-associated antigens. This program is generating compelling results in challenging cancers and is now at a development candidate stage demonstrating Phenomic’s ability to identify novel high-impact, druggable targets.

Name: GENinCode Predictive Genetics
Description:
GENinCode specializes in risk assessment and prediction of cardiovascular disease , thrombosis and familial hypercholesterolemia . Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a broad disease classification including coronary artery disease such as angina and myocardial infarction often referred to as heart attack. CVD also includes stroke, heart failure, hypertension and other vascular heart diseases and is the leading cause of death and disability worldwide accounting for 1 in every 4 deaths in the United States.

GENinCode provides advanced genomic technology, products and recommendations fully validated by our scientific and clinical team. 

Our goal is to provide doctors and health care practitioners with advanced health information that combines both traditional clinical measures with a patient’s genetic information to provide a comprehensive risk assessment and clinical recommendation to help decision-making. Our technology helps select the optimal treatment pathway and informs and educates patients to become more aware of their cardiovascular risk helping patient adherence and empowerment to better manage their health.

GENinCode technology and advanced genomic products provide information that helps patients and healthcare practitioners to assess and predict the onset of cardiovascular disease, thrombosis, and the diagnosis of Familial Hypercholesterolemia. Our online reporting system SITAB helps inform doctors of their patients’ health risk enabling patient behavioral and lifestyle changes alongside delivering the most effective therapies and treatment pathways.

Name: Solvonis Therapeutics
Description:
Solvonis Therapeutics plc (LSE: SVNS) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative medicines for addiction and mental health disorders. Headquartered in London and listed on the London Stock Exchange main market, Solvonis is advancing a differentiated pipeline of repurposed and novel compounds targeting high-burden neuropsychiatric conditions with significant unmet need.

Traditional drug development heavily relies on animal models, which often fail to accurately translate to human outcomes. This results in high failure rates in clinical trials, costly delays, and prolonged time to market for life-saving treatments. We help companies in their precision medicine design goals.

Here's why Biolligence stands out:

Human-Centric Data: Our platform generates human-relevant, population-based data, enabling more precise predictions of drug responses across diverse genetic and demographic backgrounds. This approach increases the accuracy of toxicity predictions, supporting more effective and safer clinical trial designs.

Advanced AI-Driven Insights: Leveraging cutting-edge AI algorithms, Biolligence provides deep, explainable insights into drug toxicity mechanisms. This allows researchers to uncover hidden safety liabilities early in the process, reducing the likelihood of late-stage failures and costly setbacks.

Ethical and Efficient: By reducing reliance on animal testing, we not only address ethical concerns but also offer a more efficient, scalable alternative. Our approach aligns with the global shift toward humane and sustainable research practices in drug discovery.

Precision and Speed: Our platform accelerates the path to precision-designed clinical trials, providing faster and more accurate predictions that help biopharma companies make better-informed decisions sooner. This ultimately reduces the cost and time associated with bringing safer, more effective drugs to market.

Choose Biolligence to elevate your drug discovery process with precision, reliability, and human

At the heart of our facility is a fully equipped organoid culture laboratory and ethically approved biobank, hosting over 100 intestinal organoid lines. We specialise in adult biopsy-derived intestinal models, with particular strengths in modelling infection, inflammation, and cancer, enabled by advanced readouts and integrated multi-omics analyses.

Our most recently established unit, the Centre for Intestinal Systems (CIS), is a flagship platform for gut-focused research, integrating organoids with organ-on-chip technologies and the state-of-the-art SHIME microbiome modelling system. CIS is a globally uniquely infrastructure, hosting eight complementary chip platforms, including the UK’s only HuMiX and Dynamic42 systems, as well as Europe’s first MEPSGEN ProMEPS robotic system. Description:
NanOptima is redefining ocular drug delivery through NAAmatrixTM - a natural-amino-acid, bioresorbable long-acting matrix engineered for safety, scalability, and durability.

Safe by design. Durable by nature.

NAAmatrixTM extends proven retinal drugs such as Eylea (aflibercept) and Avastin (bevacizumab) from 1–3-month dosing to beyond six-months from a single standard 30G intravitreal injection, and integrates seamlessly into current workflows for frictionless clinical adoption, requiring no devices, surgery, synthetic implants /PLGA, curing, retraining, or new equipment.

Tunable for duration, release rate, and dose, the platform is compatible across biologics, peptides, and small molecules, unlocking multi-billion-dollar lifecycle and pipeline opportunities in AMD, DME, DR, RVO, BRVO, and GA.  Recent data has demonstrated over 8-months in vitro release of TKIs.

Importantly, we believe we have already addressed many of the safety issues that have limited previous long-acting retinal platforms. Our platform is constructed entirely from natural amino-acid sequences, is designed to dissociate into low-molecular-weight peptide monomers for natural ocular clearance, has demonstrated no evidence of pro-inflammatory activation in a human retinal-cell/macrophage model, and was well tolerated in a 28-day rabbit intravitreal study.

Engineered by former AstraZeneca leaders in protein science, injectable sustained release, and CMC, and supported by clinical and regulatory KOLs, NanOptima is developing its own pipeline of long-acting therapies, and the platform itself is designed from day one for partner-ready translation and pharma collaboration to deliver strategic value to their internal pipelines.

Name: ExplantLab
Description:
What we do
ExplantLab combines extensive surgical, bioengineering and medical knowledge to understand the performance of medical implants that have been removed from the body (explants).
We do this to improve the performance of future medical devices and to protect patients from defective devices currently in use. We have a strong track record and have published over 40 scientific papers.
We are an independent company with no contracts with manufacturers - something that marks us as unique in the United Kingdom.

Understanding implant performance
At ExplantLab, we use advanced technology to reverse engineer explants in order to accurately determine their original shape. By comparing the reconstructed, original surfaces with the shape they are after removal, we can calculate how much material has been removed while in the body. This process allows us to map wear patterns and relate them to various design, patient and surgical factors.

Protecting patients and improving devices
By combining the knowledge derived from the examination of explants, ExplantLab can determine how and why those devices have performed well or poorly. This allows us to determine whether or not pre-market testing of devices is sufficiently appropriate and safe.

In providing a new class of drug to the field of antibacterial resistance, based on a truly novel mechanism of action, MGB Biopharma are unique, in that a truly new class and novel MoA was last seen in the year 2000.

There are many drugs used to treat bacterial infections, and generally they belong to classes which have been in use for several decades. Due to the rise in resistant strains of bacteria, several of these drugs are becoming less and less effective.

The Company’s progress has been rapid, and our lead drug candidate, MGB-BP-3, is currently in Phase I clinical safety studies, which will reach completion at the end of 2015. MGB-BP-3 is just the first in our new exciting class of anti-infectives.

Aqualution Systems is one of the global leaders in pathogen control. Established in 2009, Aqualution Systems Ltd is the result of eleven years of extensive scientific research, design and rigorous development which has allowed the company to reach and exceed the regulatory compliance requirements of the EU and Australasia.

Name: Cotton Mouton Diagnostics Limited
Description:
Cotton Mouton Diagnostics Ltd (CMD) is a one-stop shop for all your endotoxin testing needs. Based in Cardiff, UK, CMD are an ISO 9001 and ISO 17025 accredited company that have developed the αBET endotoxin testing system to provide end-users with a more rapid and sustainable solution to endotoxin testing without compromising on sensitivity or performance. 

The CMD αBET system is a fully integrated endotoxin testing system that delivers best-in-class sensitivity using a fraction of FDA-licensed turbidimetric LAL reagent. Quantitative results are provided in under half the time of traditional tests, with minimal user input needed beyond introduction of sample. The on-board FDA part 11 ready software package ensures data integrity, allowing users to perform pharmacopoeial compliant tests. The αBET system is suited to both in-process and final product testing across pharmaceutical manufacturing sites, quality control laboratories as well as in research and development facilities.

CMD also offer an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited endotoxin testing service, covering routine testing of all liquid pharmaceutical products including biopharmaceuticals. Certification covers method development and optimisation as well the provision of low endotoxin recovery studies.

At Priorclave Ltd, we design and manufacture research-grade autoclaves trusted by laboratories around the world. Our autoclaves are purpose-built to support critical scientific research, process development, and laboratory operations where precision, reliability, and control matter most.

From university and government research labs to pharmaceutical, biotech, and industrial research facilities, Priorclave autoclaves are engineered to adapt as your work evolves. With flexible chamber sizes, advanced programmability, and robust construction, our systems support a wide range of sterilization and research applications while scaling with your facility’s needs.

Name: Northern Light Microscopy
Description:
Northern Light Microscopy is a Glasgow‐based precision photonics company developing advanced optical imaging solutions for the life sciences.

Optical microscopy underpins almost every major biological discovery of the past century, yet access to the latest high‐ and super‐resolution imaging methods remains limited by cost, complexity and specialist infrastructure. At Northern Light Microscopy, we are changing that.

We design and build accessible advanced and super‐resolution microscopy platforms that allow researchers to extract significantly more spatial information from their samples than conventional microscopes — with no changes to established workflows. Our systems operate directly on the standard laboratory bench, removing the need for specialist facilities or expert operators.

Our flagship AMIS (Advanced Modular Imaging System) is a compact, fully enclosed benchtop microscope that integrates multiple advanced and super‐resolution imaging modes into a single platform. Powered by our patent‐pending illumination engine and controlled through our intuitive LINK software, AMIS allows users to configure, acquire and manage complex multi‐dimensional imaging experiments with ease. LINK is designed to make advanced imaging straightforward and repeatable, reducing setup time and lowering the barrier to routine use.

AMIS supports both low‐ and high‐throughput workflows, delivering enhanced spatial resolution and background rejection across everything from individual microscope slides to 96‐ and 384‐well plates. For the first time, researchers no longer have to choose between specimen throughput and spatial resolution.

By offering advanced imaging at a realistic price point, we aim to put next‐generation microscopy into the hands of the many, not just the few — empowering academic labs, biotech start‐ups and industry scientists alike.

Interested in trialling an AMIS system or learning more?

Get in touch with us at contact@northernlightmicroscopy.com

Oxford Vacmedix UK Ltd, based at the Oxford Science Park, UK, is a bio-pharma company that was spun out from the University of Oxford’s Department of Oncology and is utilising the novel proprietary platform technology of recombinant overlapping peptides (ROPs) invented by Dr Shisong Jiang. ROPs have been validated as a technology to stimulate broad and strong T cell immunity therefore forming a good platform for therapeutic vaccines and diagnostics in cancer and infectious diseases.

The technology uses the novel, proprietary platform of ROPs to design and develop therapeutic cancer vaccines and diagnostics with the potential for increased efficacy, lower costs, simpler regulatory pathways and synergy when used in combination with other immune oncology (IO) agents. The company has extensive contacts and collaborations in China through Changzhou Bioscience Group (CBIG) that is using the ROP platform for diagnostics in both cancer and in infectious diseases.

OVM is developing two lead vaccines, OVM-100 and OVM-200, focusing on unmet clinical need. OVM-100 is an HPV vaccine targeted at cervical cancer, and OVM-200 represents a new type of vaccine utilising survivin to target solid tumours. Both vaccines will be tested as single agents and in combination with IO agents. 

OVM secured Series A investment from Cancer ROP, a leading South Korean healthcare institution, listed in KOSDAQ, and from existing shareholders in China in 2018. The company is currently seeking Series B funding to advance OVM-200 to Phase 2 and OVM-100 into Phase 1 trials, as monotherapy and also in combination.

Name: Synthesea
Description:
Powered by Synthetic Biology, Synthesea is developing synthesis technology that is transferable to a wide range of lipids (AKA fats).

And we're starting with omega-3.

Omega-3 oil is a necessity for fish to grow nutritiously and is naturally found in algae, which wild fish eat. Fish grown in aquaculture (farms for fish livestock) cannot eat algae due to scaling limitations. Therefore, the current solution is to feed wild-caught fishmeal (crushed fish) to aquaculture fish. This rapidly depletes wild fish stocks and is continuously increasing the cost of omega-3 oil for aquaculture farmers.

We're using Synthetic Biology to engineer bacteria that efficiently produce cheap omega-3 oil from a plentiful precursor product. This drastically lowers costs for aquaculture farmers.

As an additional benefit, no wild fish stocks are used or harmed during this process, meaning our omega-3 oil is ecologically sustainable and ethical.

The Synthesea wound down its work at the end of 2021, and the team dissolved the company to work on other things. For more information on what Synthesea was about before it closed, you can check out our TFF entry here: https://thoughtforfood.org/synthesea/

The NanoBioTechnology Hub was founded by Dr. Alfredo Maria Gravagnuolo at Alderley Park (near Manchester) in 2025 via the Bruntwood SciTech Life Sciences Accelerator (Innovate UK-backed).

 Decentralise healthcare for a sustainable ageing society. By powering rapid point-of-care diagnostics with ultra performing nano-biomaterials and AI, we bring hospital grade performance out of the clinic and into people’s hands, reliable, affordable, and fast. Deptech Ltd is the manufacturer of the 3DEP reader; a cell analysis system that uses dielectrophoresis (DEP) to monitor cellular movement in response to different frequencies.

 Although the science underpinning DEP has been understood for decades, until now, no-one has ever been able to present it in a user-friendly, convenient and low cost package that enables any lab to take rapid, label-free cell measurements. 
For example:
Stem cells.  One of the keys to developing stem cell therapies is the rapid detection of differentiation potential well in advance of differentiation taking place. Normal protocol involves looking for surface protein biomarkers however, by the time cells have expressed the biomarkers they have already differentiated. The 3DEP Reader can detect stem cell differentiation days in advance of conventional biomarkers by looking for changes in membrane capacitance.
It’s the same with cancer – spectra obtained show DEP spectra for cancerous and healthy oral brush samples taken from the same patient. This is so accurate it’s being developed as a diagnostic technique. Moreover, recent research indicates that electrophysiological changes such as this could be a fundamental characteristic of all cancers.

Description:
Rebuilding Lives Through Medical Research
Our research helps people regain their quality of life, independence and dignity after major trauma. For more than 30 years RAFT has been focusing on research that can provide practical solutions for children and adults that through accidents, disease or birth defects can significantly benefit from our work.

Our current projects are:

Breast Reconstruction 
Our aim is to significantly improve breast reconstruction surgery as current procedures often result in an undesirable outcome and additional surgery that can last for years, leading to added pain, stress and exhaustion. We are developing techniques to vastly improve tissue transfer surgery, making it reliable and safe. 

Bone Regeneration - Beyond disability
Our research will transform the way we currently treat patients that need replacement bone. Current methods involve invasive and painful bone grafts that are not always successful or possible. RAFT’s method of placing a biological scaffold on the damaged area to stimulate bone growth will enable new bone to grow and fill the damaged area perfectly.

Keloid Scars - Preventing recurrence
RAFT is working on the development of a dermal scaffold intended for use after surgical excision of a keloid. A dermal scaffold is a type of treatment used by surgeons, which acts as a template to guide the growth of new skin at a wound site and avoid scarring. RAFT's scaffold will be specifically designed to inhibit the recurrence of keloid scarring.

3D Printing for Craniofacial Surgery
We are undertaking research to develop a new type of material specifically for 3D printing to create custom-fit facial implants. Digital models will be created from X-rays and CT scans, which will be used to develop bespoke 3D implants that once fitted, will create a scaffold that will encourage the patient’s own bone to grow to the required shape and size. Name: Onya Therapeutics
Description:
Chronic wounds remain one of healthcare's most under-recognised mortality burdens. In diabetic foot ulceration, five-year mortality is estimated at around 30%, and can exceed 70% after major amputation — placing severe wound complications in the same mortality conversation as many cancers.

Yet wound care is still too often treated as a secondary category. In the last 25 years, more than 250 new drugs have been approved for cancer. The FDA has approved approximately two pharmaceutical wound healing treatments in the same period. The standard of care for chronic wounds remains absorbent dressings — devices that manage symptoms without addressing the underlying pathology.

ONYA Therapeutics is building a new pharmaceutical category for the treatment of chronic and acute wounds.

We call it Active Exudate Therapy (AET): the medicinal modulation of wound exudate at source, designed to resolve chronic inflammation and restart physiological healing. AET is not an iteration on existing products. It is a fundamentally different approach.

Our lead investigational programme, OTX-PP01, is a medicated patch in development for chronic wound indications including diabetic foot ulcers, venous leg ulcers and pressure ulcers. It is designed for application during a routine dressing change — no retraining, no new equipment, no incremental nurse time.

OTX-PP01 is the lead programme on a patented platform designed to support several significant further indications over time, including military applications.

Our Clinical Advisory Board is chaired by Professor Steven Jeffery, alongside Jacqui Fletcher OBE, Professor Karen Ousey, Dr Thomas Serena, Professor Keith Harding CBE and Breda Cullen PhD.

Headquartered in Ebbw Vale, Wales. Engaging clinicians, partners and investors globally.

Name: ModelMole
Description:
ModelMole is an AI drug discovery company developing an autonomous, infrastructure-agnostic platform for molecular design and optimisation. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in the United Kingdom, the company combines physics-based computational chemistry with state-of-the-art machine learning to discover novel therapeutic candidates that lie beyond the reach of conventional AI approaches.
The platform is built around a proprietary swarm AI system that orchestrates multiple models in parallel, cross-referencing predictions to quantify confidence and automatically filling data gaps using molecular dynamics, quantum mechanical, and docking calculations. An automatic active learning loop iteratively improves predictions with every problem solved, enabling the platform to "look into the dark" — exploring sparse regions of chemical space where traditional ML models fail.
ModelMole is fully autonomous and infrastructure-agnostic, designed to run on environments ranging from enterprise compute clusters to a single workstation. The platform supports the full discovery pipeline — drug design, delivery, formulation, stability, and optimisation — and is currently used by clients in oncology, antimicrobial development, regenerative medicine, and cosmetics.
The company's research is published in leading peer-reviewed journals including the Royal Society of Chemistry's PCCP, the Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters, Cell, and Angewandte Chemie. Active programmes include targeted radiotheranostics for oncology, antimicrobial peptides and peptide-drug conjugates, transcription regulator discovery, and collagen repair peptides for soft tissue regeneration.
ModelMole is supported by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and works with academic partners including the Royal Society of Chemistry. Model Mole Ltd is registered in England and Wales (No. 14909542).

Name: Arborcheck
Description:
Arborcheck systems are designed specifically for arborists. Quick and easy, non-destructive physiological assessments of tree health are made using hand-held, cost effective instruments based on proven scientific techniques which have been and continue to be widely used in photosynthesis research the world over. The system has been developed in response to the scale in which chlorophyll fluorescence is gaining popularity with arborists around the world as an effective and comprehensive method of assessing tree health.

Readings taken by Arborcheck systems are compared to a species specific Nursery Benchmark Database which has been independently compiled and verified by Dr. Glynn Percival and colleagues from  Bartlett Tree Research Laboratories based on identical measurements made annually since 2009 on trees grown in optimum conditions at the Barcham Trees nursery in the UK. The Nursery Benchmark Database currently contains optimum photosynthetic efficiency, vitality and chlorophyll content values from more than 600,000 individual leaf sample measurements taken from more than 350 tree species.

Arborcheck systems can be used effectively in many areas of arboriculture from the selection of physiologically sound planting stock through to quantitative assessment of stress in veteran trees on development sites. The techniques used by Arborcheck systems are scientifically proven to allow early detection of severely damaging stress factors well before visible symptoms are apparent. Arborcheck systems can also indicate a sound physiological framework on a tree that looks visibly in poor condition. Prompt and efficient remediation in these cases can often lead to a swift recovery of a tree that may otherwise have been felled based on a visual analysis.

Chlorophyll fluorescence testing is also cited in the new British Standard BS 8545: Trees: from nursery to independence in the landscape as a recommended tool for ongoing monitoring of tree health post-planting.

Description:
Elastin Biosciences is a London-based biopharma company focused on the development of small molecule therapies to treat diseases and conditions linked to the loss of elastin. Elastin has pioneered a combination approach using small molecules to recover elastin deposition and inhibit its degradation. Elastin is a vital protein in the human body that imparts elasticity and resilience to various tissues, such as the skin, lungs, and blood vessels. Elastin degrades over time due to aging, leading to a loss of tissue elasticity and function, which is associated with numerous age-related diseases.
The Company’s Elastin Restoration Platform leverages a combination of proprietary small molecules designed to fortify the structural integrity of crucial tissues, including those in the cardiovascular and epidermal systems, by inhibiting elastin degradation and increasing elastin production. Elastin’s lead development program, currently completing in vivo proof-of-concept, has demonstrated an ability to increase elastin expression and arterial tensile strength in models of abdominal aortic aneurism and Williams syndrome, a rare a multisystem disorder characterized by elastin arteriopathy, most often manifesting as supravalvuar aortic stenosis.

Name: NanoGenics
Description:
Nanogenics is a UK research based virtual biotechnology company.  Founded to develop the LipTideTM nanoformulation platform, the focus now is on developing product ECP105 through preclinical and towards clinical testing.

ECP105 is under development for the treatment of Glaucoma patients undergoing trabeculectomy surgery.  This surgical technique relieves intra-ocular pressure by creating a channel into which the eye drains.  Although well established and successful, surgical failure can occur if the surgical wound undergoes fibrosis and the scar prevents drainage.

The active ingredient of ECP105 is an siRNA designed to down-regulate a gene involved in scarring and fibrosis.  Using a single sub-conjunctival injection of ECP105 during trabeculectomy surgery the risk of scarring will be lowered leading to improved surgical outcomes and reduced need for repeat surgery.

Presented in the LipTideTM formulation, ECP105 targets the relevant cells of the eye in a safe and predictable manner.

LipTideTM is a peptide nanoparticle that has already shown excellent in vivo efficacy across a range of models and delivery routes, including nebulised and systemic administration.  This targeted, receptor-mediated, active uptake means that LipTideTM can be used to deliver any type of nucleic acid payload, including gene editing tools and nucleic acid vaccines.

LipTideTM is available as a platform to encapsulate DNA and RNA with the patented lipid/peptide formulation.  Nanogenics is interested in meeting potential clinical investment partners to discuss licencing opportunities for LipTideTM.

Name: Bio-Analysis Centre - HPLC & Mass Spectrometry Analysis Consultancy or Bespoke Training
Description:
The Bio-Analysis Centre offers Triple Quad Mass Spectrometry, advanced HPLC plus the latest High Performance label free Capillary Electrophoresis (HPCE) system from deltaDOT. With these instruments we can assist in identifying and quantitating a wide range of analytes through contract research - based on over 20 years experience, offering both Academia and Industry a fully comprehensive service. 
With regard to our services, we use the Shimadzu Nexera XR HPLC system and the Shimadzu LCMS-8040. The HPLC's have cooled autosamplers and Photo-Diode Array detectors, which can be used for compound analysis from small molecules to proteins. 
Our LCMS system provides highly sensitive, reliable and fast results. Analysis of both positive and negative ions is possible in the same experiment due to fast polarity switching capabilities – allowing for simultaneous analysis, and its ability to do quantitation with good linearity makes this an ideal instrument for drug studies.
For our HPCE service, we use one of deltaDOT’s latest instruments (HPCE-512), which separates and analyses a wide range of samples - from small molecules and amino acids, through to proteins and virus-like particles. It uses an advanced form of label free CE which produces faster, higher quality results at a fraction of the cost of many other approaches.
We are aspiring to GLP compliance so that we will be able to meet a wider range of clients’ analytical requirements.
In addition to providing an analytical service, we also offer training on the Shimadzu Nexera XR HPLC and the Shimadzu LCMS-8040 systems. Once training has been completed, clients will receive in-house certification, allowing them to use our equipment to run their own samples.
This cost-effective service gives clients more control over their research and allows them to work at their own pace. Although clients will be fully responsible for conducting their own work, there will always be a laboratory assistant available to help if needed.

Name: Edinburgh Metabolism
Description:
Edinburgh Metabolism, within the newly formed Institute for Neuroscience and Cardiovascular Research (INCR) at the University of Edinburgh, brings together basic and clinical scientists dedicated to understanding and improving metabolic health. We focus on cutting-edge research to explore how metabolic processes support health, how they fail and lead to disease, and how novel approaches can reduce risk and improve treatments for metabolic disorders.

Our work is centered on three key areas of research:

Mechanisms of Metabolic Health:
We investigate the biological processes that maintain metabolic health across the lifespan. Understanding these mechanisms is critical for identifying ways to protect and promote metabolic function.

 
Disruptions in Metabolic Processes:
Our research focuses on how these mechanisms go awry to contribute to conditions such as obesity, diabetes, fatty liver disease, cardiovascular diseases, and increased vulnerability to infections.

Innovative Approaches for Disease Prevention and Treatment:
We are dedicated to developing novel strategies for reducing disease risk and improving treatment outcomes for established metabolic diseases, paving the way for better healthcare solutions.


We maintain close collaborations across the University of Edinburgh, particularly through the Edinburgh Diabetes Network, and with the Institute for Regeneration and Repair, the Institute of Genetics and Cancer, The Usher Institute, Edinburgh Neuroscience, and the Edinburgh Pregnancy Research Team.  We benefit from a range of strong international collaborations, especially with Denmark (through the Danish Diabetes and Endocrine Academy, DDEA) and Malawi (through NIHR funding).

Our position in the Edinburgh BioQuarter campus seeds strong interactions with data scientists within the Usher Institute/DataLoch. Our wider outreach also includes links with One Health programmes in the veterinary campus (LARIF).

S. M. Discovery Group (SMDG) is redefining the future of precision medicine by addressing one of the greatest challenges in modern therapeutics: delivering the right treatment to the right cells, at the right time.

Despite remarkable advances in biology and drug discovery, millions of patients living with neurological, rare, inflammatory, and other complex diseases continue to face limited treatment options. For many of these conditions, the greatest obstacle is not identifying a promising therapeutic—it is delivering that therapeutic safely, precisely, and effectively to its intended target.

At SMDG, we believe overcoming this challenge has the potential to transform the treatment of disease.

Our proprietary platform technologies have been engineered to enable targeted delivery of advanced therapeutics, including to tissues protected by biological barriers such as the brain. By integrating peptide engineering, nanotechnology, molecular biology, artificial intelligence, and translational science, we are developing next-generation platforms designed to support precision delivery, improve therapeutic performance, and accelerate the development of disease-modifying medicines.

Beyond therapeutic delivery, we are advancing biomarker discovery to help improve diagnosis, patient stratification, therapeutic selection, and the development of precision medicine approaches. Together, these complementary technologies provide an integrated framework for discovering, developing, and translating innovative therapies from the laboratory to the clinic.

Scientific excellence, innovation, and collaboration are central to everything we do. Our distilling product has been rigorously tested by leading UK distillers, repeatedly demonstrating an impressive 10%-20% increase in alcohol yield and a reduction in process time of >40%. 

Environmental & social impact is central to our mission. Annually, a staggering 30 million tons of bananas are discarded into landfill, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to 400 million tons of CO2. Farmers bear the burden of unsellable crops without receiving compensation. LyteGro aims to transform this situation by utilising waste banana feedstock and converting it into valuable products, simultaneously addressing environmental concerns and supporting farmers by paying for their otherwise discarded waste.

Our overarching focus is accelerating the global transition to a sustainable and circular economy. By enabling end users to enhance the efficiency of their green chemistry and bio-based industrial processes with our products, we contribute to a more sustainable future.

Name: Prosemble
Description:
The targeted delivery of therapeutic molecules to specific cells and tissue, is probably the biggest challenge in modern medicine. 
Most drugs are delivered through the systemic blood circulation, and consequently the vast majority of therapeutic agents never reach the affected organs. This often leads to very low efficacy, and/or side effects. For example, it is estimated that in chemotherapy treatments, 99% of anticancer molecules never reach the tumour cite. 

At ProSemble, we use a proprietary technology to design new protein-based biomaterials, whose assembly and disassembly can be chemically controlled. This will be used for drug reformulation, to improve efficacy, and reduce side-effects, of existing drugs. 
In particular, we have developed a protein nanocage which can incorporate the anticancer drug doxorubicin, and release it in the vicinity of tumour cells. We will develop this towards the treatment of breast cancer.

Name: Antigonie Biosciences
Description:
Antigonie Biosciences has engineered a targeted gene therapy platform - Asteria - to create next-generation anti-cancer RNA therapeutics for blood cancers. 

We are moving hemato-oncology from lifelong management to potentially curative strategies through the creation of therapeutics that can eliminate the root of blood cancers: malignant HSPCs.

In contrast to systemic chemotherapy regimens that treat the consequence of blood cancer - an overproduction of mature blood cells - but not the cause, our RNA therapeutics deliver to malignant HSPCs in the bone marrow.

The platform delivers mutation-specific RNAi designed with high specificity to silence the mutant genes (e.g., JAK2V617F) that cause hematologic malignancies in HSPCs. Our therapeutics “shoot the messenger” by eliminating mutant messenger RNA (mRNA). Their specificity means they completely spare the healthy gene mRNA, minimizing off-target effects in healthy cells.

By successfully delivering a selective killing agent to the root disease-initiating cells (HSPCs), our platform triggers mutation-specific cell death. Our therapeutics induce the functional depletion and eradication of the malignant HSPC clone.

W-0301 - Platform validation in MPNs: Our lead candidate, W-0301, targeting JAK2V617F Myeloproliferative Neoplasms (MPNs), is successful proof-of-concept for our platform technology. W-0301's strong preclinical profile, recently presented in an oral presentation at a global hematology conference, validates our ability to safely and effectively deliver genetic payloads to the challenging bone marrow environment. This success accelerates the development of our entire pipeline.

The Expanding Pipeline: Asteria, our validated LNP platform, allows us to rapidly target other prevalent somatic mutations and oncogenic drivers across the spectrum of hematologic malignancies.

Description:

In the world of bioproduction, precise control of growth conditions is well-recognized as essential for successfully maximizing the yield and quality of products from microbial cultures. However, equipment complexity and costs associated with using large-scale bioreactors made it seemingly impossible to achieve similar success at smaller scales in the research laboratory. Then Dr. Peter Neubauer and his team decided to attempt the impossible and the idea behind the patented EnBase technology was born.
Founded in 2007 in Oulu, Finland, BioSilta is now headquartered in Cambridge, UK. The company, comprised of a multi-national group of individuals with collectively over 150 years of experience in the biotech industry, is financed by the investment companies, Omega Funds, Inveni Capital and Oulun Seudun Hyvinvointirahasto.

Today, the company’s customers are found mainly in life science research and BioSilta scientists focus their expertise on expanding the range of game-changing EnPresso growth systems.

Today, BioSilta scientists focus their expertise on utilizing the unique EnBase technology platform to develop game-changing EnPresso reagent-based, growth systems that control microbial growth. TauC3 Biologics is developing a disease-modifying treatment for tauopathies, including frontotemporal dementia due to tau pathology (FTD-tau) and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP). Brain examination reveals abnormal deposits of tau protein that are believed to be preceded by toxic, soluble forms that lead to neuronal death. Currently in preclinical development, the company’s therapeutic candidate, TBL-100, is a humanized monoclonal antibody that uniquely targets a truncated form of tau known as tauC3 that appears to be highly elevated in these conditions. TauC3, is by far the most noxious form of tau due to its heightened propensity to aggregate, promote spread of tau pathology through the brain, and impair the delivery of mitochondria and other essential cellular constituents to synapses. TauC3’s ability to cause normal tau to aggregate confers enormous potential amplification causing extensive cellular damage. TBL-100 has 1000-fold specificity for tauC3 compared to normal tau and is believed to act at least in part by promoting clearance of tauC3 from the brain. In addition to its therapeutic potential, TBL-100’s specificity may enable use as a diagnostic agent for tauopathies, a critical tool that is currently lacking. 

Bringing together world-class expertise and drug development talent to turn its vision into a reality, TauC3 Biologics is poised for efficient preclinical development and subsequent early clinical development, with the aim of rapidly demonstrating safety and proof of concept.

Name: Bio4Products project
Description:
The Bio4Products project will show how bio-resources can be converted into renewable alternatives to fossil-based processing streams such as bitumen, phenols and creosote. The project will demonstrate the integration of these sustainable resources into four end products: roofing material, phenolic resins, sand moulding resins, and engineered wood and natural fibre reinforced products.

The Bio4Products project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement No. 723070.

Innovative biomass conversion
Bio4Products will demonstrate an innovative two-step conversion method based on thermal fractionation. Treatment by fast pyrolysis will first convert the solid biomass into a bio-oil, while largely preserving the original functionalities. The next step sees the functional groups present in the bio-oil separated by fractionation, obtaining a sugar stream and a lignin stream. A fractionation demo-plant will be constructed by BTG Biomass Technology group at their facility in the Netherlands.

New bio-based products 
Bio4Products will create renewable and natural alternatives to fossil-based processing streams such as bitumen, phenols and creosote. Partners will demonstrate the integration of these sustainable resources into four end products: 
1. roofing material
2. phenolic resins 
3. sand moulding resins 
4. engineered wood and natural fibre reinforced products

The overall objective is to create four products, which, due to the replacement of fossil materials with bio-based resources, deliver a 75% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.

Name: Geodesic Labs
Description:
We generate therapeutic assets by leveraging our proprietary Causal AI and patient-derived single-cell interventional data.

Pharma's discovery methods are indirect, because they had to be. Mouse models, genetic correlation, and pathway inference became standard because interventional data straight from human cells didn't exist at scale until recently. None of them answer the question the clinic ultimately asks: what happens when you hit this gene, in this person. That gap is why most drug programs fail, at a cost of hundreds of millions each. We generate that data directly in patient cells, and use causal AI to build a working model of human biology from it.

Sparse evidence means everyone converges on the same handful of targets. Because so few targets ever look de-risked enough to pursue, competition for them is fierce. Our causal models trace the regulatory network upstream of those crowded targets, to the master regulators actually driving them: novel targets nobody else can see. And because we model the full causal path, not just the target itself, we can see what hitting that gene does downstream, including where it's likely to cause toxicity, before a single compound is made.

Most AI predicts. Drug discovery requires intervention. Standard models learn what tends to move together, not what happens if you change one thing. Ask them an interventional question anyway, and they answer confidently and wrong. But "what happens if you hit this gene, with this drug, in this patient" is exactly the question drug discovery needs answered. Our causal AI is built to answer it directly, not approximate it from correlation.

Modern drug discovery has benefitted enormously from advances in human genomics. IOTA uses transcriptomics to provide individually-tailored gene family-based drug discovery platforms to address the involvement of specific members of gene families in human disease.

Our current therapeutic focus is glioblastoma. Glioblastoma is a brain cancer that typically attacks adults at the peak of their working lives and family responsibilities. Other cancers have been ameliorated or cured by modern medicine, but no currently available treatment, either chemical or surgical, appreciably slows the progression of glioblastoma, which is invariably fatal.

There is an urgent need for fresh approaches to this intractable cancer. Glioblastoma tumours are unresponsive to our current generalised weaponry of chemotherapy. IOTA has the ability to turn this promise into clinical efficacy in a reasonable timescale by using the tools we already have to hand in transformative ways.

IOTA has developed a suite of transcriptomics-based diagnostics that compare and contrast drug-treated, patient-derived tumour cells, looking in detail at the drug targets that they express, and defining specific FDA-approved drugs that could be used immediately in treatment strategies in the clinic.

Unlike antibiotics, Battlestar targets multiple cellular pathways, preventing resistance while combating infections. It safely and stably delivers oxidative biocides, offering broad-spectrum antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity while supporting healing.

•	Broad-spectrum activity: Effectively targets bacteria, viruses, fungi, and biofilms, providing robust antimicrobial and antibiofilm action.
•	Tissue-friendly technology: Encapsulation in PLGA minimises cytotoxicity while releasing healing agents like lactate to support tissue regeneration.

•	Biocompatibility: Decomposes into water, oxygen, lactic acid, and glycolic acid—naturally processed by the body to create an environment that supports healing.

Battlestar is more than a technology; it’s a solution to AMR, designed to transform infection management across multiple healthcare sectors—including wound care, biofilm-associated tumours, urinary tract infections, and osteomyelitis—while preserving antibiotics, protecting patients, and preventing resistance.

Chiralabs provides world-leading specialist consultancy, contract research and analytical services for investigating molecular products in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology and chemical industries. A wide range of spectroscopic, physicochemical and theoretical approaches are undertaken to enhance the discovery, development and manufacture of products ranging from small molecular drugs through to biopharmaceuticals, proteins and DNA. 

Specialist areas include crystallization, molecular chirality, protein/DNA folding & properties and spectroscopic/physicochemical characterisation (circular dichroism a speciality). Chiralabs invented the internationally award winning CrystalGEM technology for the efficient screening of pharmaceutical crystallization and has pioneered the spectroscopic fingerprinting of biopharmaceuticals for comparability, biosimilarity and troubleshooting. 

Core to the rational drug discovery process is the understanding of phenomena at the molecular level by the complementary combination of both experimental and theoretical approaches in unison, a principle Chiralabs promotes.

Name: decyte
Description:
Late cancer diagnosis remains one of the leading drivers of cancer-related mortality. For most cancers survival drops dramatically as the disease progresses - highlighting the urgent need for reliable, early detection. Despite clear benefits, existing screening methods are often invasive, unpleasant, insufficiently sensitive in early stages, or poorly adopted, leaving a critical gap in care.

Decyte is addressing this gap by developing a non-invasive, affordable technology for early detection of solid tumours. Rather than relying on direct detection of tumour-derived material in blood - which typically appears only in later stages - decyte decodes the immune system’s response to cancer, an early and systemic signal present from the onset of disease. By harnessing this immune signature, decyte aims to make early cancer screening straightforward, accessible, and clinically impactful, when treatment can still meaningfully improve outcomes.

Name: EVolution Therapeutics Ltd
Description:
We are EVolution Therapeutics, an innovative biotech spin-out from Aston University with a visionary mission: to redefine the treatment of inflammatory disease by harnessing the body’s own resolution and repair pathways.

Inflammation is essential for survival — but when the body fails to resolve it, it can become a driver of tissue damage, impaired healing and chronic disease. Across conditions such as non-healing wounds, inflammatory skin disease, pulmonary disease, fibrosis and cardiovascular disease, unresolved inflammation remains a major cause of patient suffering, healthcare burden and unmet clinical need.

Current anti-inflammatory treatments often focus on suppressing inflammatory signals. While this can provide short-term relief, it does not always restore the biological processes needed to resolve inflammation and repair damaged tissue.

At EVolution Therapeutics, we are taking a different approach.

Our local mRNA-LNP hydrogel platform is designed to deliver pro-resolving biology directly to diseased tissue, shifting the local environment away from chronic inflammation and towards repair, regeneration and restored function.

Our lead programme focuses on chronic non-healing wounds — a visible, measurable and high-need clinical entry point for our broader inflammation-resolution platform. But our ambition extends far beyond wounds.

Built on pioneering academic research from Professor Andrew Devitt’s group at Aston University, EVolution Therapeutics is translating decades of inflammation and extracellular vesicle biology into a new generation of pro-resolution therapeutics.

 Let’s Connect and Innovate

We believe collaboration is the driving force behind breakthrough healthcare innovation. If you share our passion for transforming inflammatory disease treatment, or have opportunities for investment, partnership or strategic collaboration, let’s connect.

Together, we can help move medicine beyond inflammation suppression — and towards true resolution.

Medicine is on the edge of its largest shift.
For a century we have fought disease one pathology at a time. Each therapy a separate battle, each win narrow. That era built modern medicine. It will not build what comes next.
Something more fundamental is now within reach. Beneath most of the diseases we fear sits a shared cause: the progressive loss of cellular function. Restore that function and you are no longer treating a single disease. You are addressing the conditions that give rise to many at once.
This is not an incremental improvement on existing medicine. It is a new category of it. A shift from managing decline to reversing it. From one target at a time to the system itself.
BioRes exists to make that shift real. We are building toward therapeutics that restore cellular function safely and controllably, so that health becomes something we can rebuild at its foundation rather than something we slowly lose.
If this can be done, and done safely, it will be among the most consequential things medicine has ever achieved.
We are building for the people who already see it.

Description:
Mission: Deliver low-cost, non-invasive in vitro diagnostics (IVDs) for high-incidence diseases at the point-of-care.

Approach: Using Raman Spectroscopy and Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) to achieve detection beyond current standard-of-care IVDs. Existing research supports identifying target diseases in urine using this approach.

Focus: Serox has attracted a fantastic array of scientific and medical advisors and has established clinical relationships to help validate its approach, initially in bladder, prostate and kidney cancers. The intention is to ‘bundle’ tests which may be requested together, say when a patient presents with blood in their urine.  Women’s cancers will follow, along with point-of-care speciation of Urinary Tract Infections. 

Differentiation: Serox displaces chemistry with photonics and Machine Learning, to allow urinalysis to avoid invasive procedures (blood taking, biopsy cystoscopy). Serox is following a data-focussed path that will lead to the personalisation of IVD.

Timeliness: Raman Spectroscopy and SERS have long been used in advanced laboratories. The price of lasers and detectors is falling, and the usability and deployability of Raman Spectrometer improving. Machine Learning allows the ability to diagnose from the aggregate of Raman shifts in complex liquids. Together this unlocks the use of Raman Spectroscopy as a routine diagnostic.

Outcome: Serox offers the prospect of a low-cost cartridge that be used remotely to acquire a urine sample, or in a clinic at the point-of-care, that can be processed using a desktop analyser in less than three minutes to provide an answer with a high Negative Predictive Value, and sensitivity / specificity in line with the current standard-of-care. This could reduce referrals to cystoscopy and biopsy, ultimately transform screening, and reduce the unnecessary use of broad-spectrum antimicrobials.

Name: Biodetection Technologies Hub
Description:
Bioaerosols – airborne particles of biological origin, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, pollen, and toxins – are among our atmosphere's most ubiquitous, complex components. They can spread disease, compromise food security, infiltrate the respiratory system, and be weaponised in biowarfare. They can even influence cloud formation, shaping weather patterns and climate. Despite their significance, real-time detection of bioaerosols is underdeveloped, and existing monitoring systems are rarely deployed at scale.
The Biodetection Technologies Hub is closing this gap. We are developing cutting-edge detection systems that can rapidly identify and quantify bioaerosols across multiple environments, from hospitals and military settings to farms and high in the Earth’s atmosphere. Our vision is to enable near-real-time biodetection, supporting faster responses to airborne threats and building safer, healthier, and more resilient environments.
Led by the University of Hertfordshire’s Wolfson Centre for Research in Biodetection Technologies and supported by Cranfield University, the University of Leeds, and the University of Manchester, the Hub unites leading experts in engineering, aerosol science, microbiology, chemistry, atmospheric science, AI-driven analytics, and sensor technology. Description:
Since 2024 BioMoti is no longer active; this is an historical page.


Ovarian cancer is an extremely deadly disease characterised by an abnormal growth of ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal tissue with malignant tumours spreading beyond the site of origin into the peritoneal cavity and affecting the organs within (e.g. the spleen, bowel mesentery and liver). There were nearly 300,000 new cases of ovarian cancer worldwide in 2018 [World Cancer Research Fund]. For most patients, surgery is the first line of treatment. This is usually followed by chemotherapy and typically devastating side effects including hair loss, nausea, vomiting, appetite loss, pain, weakened immunity and fatigue.

We are developing #Oncojans, a promising new class of drug-loaded particles, designed to precisely target and gain entry to cancer cells. In the tumours, they slowly release drugs at the point of need whilst sparing healthy tissue. Early preclinical studies for #BMT101, our lead ovarian cancer candidate, compared to the clinical standard of care, Taxol, have shown very encouraging results including over 10-fold increases in drug concentration in tumours, 65-fold reductions in tumour burden, doubling of median survival and loss of toxicity. #BMT101 and future engineered #Oncojans could be transformational in the treatment of cancer patients.

The Problem: Drug Discovery's Fundamental Challenges
Traditional drug development is inefficient, costly, and fails in over 90% of cases—primarily because early predictions rarely translate to clinical success
Current computational approaches like AlphaFold 3 excel at modeling specific interactions (like drug-protein binding) but fail to capture the intricate network of biological interactions that determine real-world therapeutic outcomes
Promising candidates routinely fail in late-stage clinical trials due to unforeseen toxicity or limited efficacy, after substantial investment
The Solution: A Programmable Virtual Human (PVH)
PVH creates comprehensive simulations of human biology that enable researchers to:
Predict therapeutic responses with unprecedented accuracy before entering clinical testing
Identify potential adverse effects and toxicity profiles during early development stages
Engineer molecules with optimized therapeutic indices—maximizing efficacy while minimizing harm
Close the critical gap between preclinical research and clinical outcomes

By integrating advances in artificial intelligence, high-throughput experimental biology, single-cell analytics, and real-world evidence, PVH functions as a "biological compiler" for drug discovery. Rather than iterating through countless design cycles, it systematically identifies the optimal therapeutic intervention to restore homeostasis based on sophisticated virtual human mode

Inexia is developing intranasal orexin receptor agonists and positive modulators for the treatment of narcolepsy, a rare neurological condition that affects the brain's ability to regulate the normal sleep-wake cycle

Orexin agonists and positive modulators will directly address the underlying disease pathology of NT1, and may have the potential for greater efficacy and tolerability than current therapies.

Despite advances in assisted reproductive technologies, implantation failure and poor endometrial receptivity continue to limit success rates. LYMPHOGENiX was founded to address this unmet need by targeting a fundamental but overlooked component of reproductive biology.

Our core scientific insight is that lymphatic vessels play a critical role in endometrial function, tissue homeostasis, and immune regulation, all of which are essential for successful embryo implantation. By modulating lymphangiogenesis and lymphatic function within the endometrium, we aim to create a new therapeutic paradigm to improve implantation rates and reproductive outcomes.

Infertility is LYMPHOGENiX’s lead therapeutic programme and primary clinical focus. Our pipeline is being advanced through robust preclinical validation, including translational models bridging large-animal and human biology. This approach is designed to de-risk development and accelerate progression toward clinical application.

While infertility is our clear commercial and clinical priority, our underlying lymphatic biology platform has broader relevance across multiple disease areas. Ongoing academic collaborations allow us to explore these opportunities at a foundational research level, without diluting strategic focus.

LYMPHOGENiX operates at the intersection of vascular biology, reproductive medicine, and translational science. We work with leading academic groups, CRO partners, and international stakeholders to ensure scientific rigor, reproducibility, and a clear path to patients.

Our mission is simple and focused: to translate lymphatic biology into meaningful clinical solutions for infertility

Look at Gel Documentation – the new Vü

Pop Bio has developed an exciting new system for the image capture and analysis of gels and blots. The innovative Vü imaging system opens up a new era for gel documentation.

Vü Imaging is no ordinary gel documentation system however. The Pop Bio Vü Imaging system uses no cameras, no lenses, filters, or lasers but instead utilizes a new technology to accurately map images at ultra-high sensitivity and resolution. The result is a small desk top instrument with a very small footprint that can handle the full range of gel and blot applications – UV, blue light, visible and chemiluminescence. The Advanced Progressive Imaging technology, which was developed in Cambridge, is a clever use of imaging sensors that accurately map low levels of light from any gel or blot. A patent for this new technology has been applied for. 

Aside from the new technology being used in the instrument the cost is also considerably lower than that of a traditional gel documentation system which uses high cost CCD cameras, lenses and filters. The Pop Bio Vü Imaging system aims to become the new standard for gel and blot image capture and replace existing traditional gel documentation systems over the next few years. This device is destined to change the way images of gels and blots are captured.

Two variants of the instrument have been launched. The Vü-F is for fluorescence applications like Etbr DNA gels using UV or safe dyes using blue light as well as visible light protein gels and blots. The Vü-C has increased sensitivity for chemiluminescent western blots.

Name: Oxford Structural Proteomics for Biomedical Research
Description:
The Oxford Structural & Mechanistic Proteomics Laboratory is based within the Centre for Medicines Discovery (CMD), University of Oxford. The lab is headed by Dr Darragh O'Brien.

We are a team of structural biologists who use Hydrogen/Deuterium eXchange Mass Spectrometry (HDX-MS) to provide unique insights into how proteins are shaped and how they function. The unique selling point of HDX-MS over analogous structural techniques such as X-ray crystallography and Cryo-EM is that it provides dynamic insights into macromolecular interactions, rather than static snapshots. Essentially, how proteins “dance” in solution.

HDX-MS is used for:
•	Deciphering conformational changes in complexes
•	Locating and characterising binding sites
•	Determining protein solution dynamics
•	Untangling protein folding pathways
•	Characterising protein intrinsic disorder

HDX-MS applications include:
•	Epitope Mapping
•	Drug Development
•	Biomarker Characterisation
•	Protein Stability Studies
•	Small-molecule Screening

The Oxford Structural & Mechanistic Proteomics Laboratory is fully-equipped to undertake cutting-edge structural proteomics experiments, housing a LEAP HDX Automation Robot (Trajan) and an Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific).

For collaboration enquiries, or a chat about how HDX-MS can help with your research, feel free to get in touch.

Name: Switch Biologics
Description:
Switch Biologics is building logic-gated enzyme therapies for late-stage cancer.
Targeted oncology suffers from a toxicity ceiling: ADCs, BiTEs, and even masked antibodies cannot cleanly separate tumour from healthy tissue when the antigen is shared, and on-target/off-tumour toxicity keeps the most potent targets out of reach. Our enzymes operate as AND-gates, requiring two tumour-specific inputs for activation, and reversibly switch off when disengaged — inactive in circulation, catalytic inside the tumour.
The result is high therapeutic fidelity and a therapeutic window wide enough to address antigens the field has had to deprioritise.

Name: Genetix
Description:
More than just a defect......

Mould is not merely a building defect, it is a public health issue with potentially serious consequences for occupants.

Since the introduction of Awaab's Law, housing providers carry enhanced legal duties to identify, investigate, and remediate damp and mould promptly and effectively. However, understanding what the presence of mould actually means for the health of each individual occupant is complex and cannot be determined by property inspection alone.


Why Genetix?

Genetix provides clear, defensible risk assessments by integrating property specific sampling, environmental science and medical insight. Our multidisciplinary approach ensures that the correct skills are called upon at each stage in the process through our trusted supply chain. We do this because we believe the determination of health risks associated with indoor mould exposure cannot be completed though a single professional lens.

The result is a robust, evidence-based assessment that goes beyond identifying mould presence, considering the specific fungal species present in the property and the health history of each individual occupant before any decision is made on how that mould needs to be dealt with.

Description:
Founded in October 2021, the Oxford Biomedical Imaging Society (OBIS) aims to support the development, improvement and promotion of interdisciplinary thinking and networking in the field of biomedical imaging.
