Name: Genetrainer
Description:
Genetically guided fitness. Genetrainer provides people with personalised training plans, exercises and advice developed from their own DNA and it gives people a faster and more measurable way of achieving their individual training goals.

Heart rate, sleep and weight can all be tracked, so people can monitor their progress and fitness in real time. The system enables people’s training plans and advice to be automatically synchronised with their body condition and current fitness level.

Genetrainer is compatible with a range of popular commercial genetic tests. People simply select their fitness goals and their results and plan are generated computationally personalised to their genetic constitution.

Name: CCA Bio
Description: CCA Bio builds infrastructure for modern biology. We integrate lab operations, hardware, telemetry, and software into a single ecosystem system that turns biological experiments into structured, machine-readable records by default. By keeping protocol state, measurements, and environmental context linked from the moment data is generated, we help labs improve reproducibility, traceability, and decision-making across research and scale-up workflows. From continuous environmental monitoring with Pebble to protocol-linked experiment infrastructure in CCA Labs, we’re building the data foundation for the next generation of biology.

Name: xRapid Foundation
Description:
xRapid is a world first in mobile health, it is the first commercially available app that has the functionality to quickly and accurately diagnose a major disease.

By deploying cutting edge Digital Imaging technology and Artificial Intelligence, xRapid has brought a revolutionary diagnostic platform that can diagnose diseases such as Malaria faster, cheaper and more accurately than conventional methods. The test is accurate to a minimum of 98%, is consistent and reliable in its results as well as robust enough to cope with harsh climates and hot temperatures. Added to all of this, it is the lowest cost per test on the global market.

The company has first developed xRapid-Malaria, an app that empowers health workers in the field and in laboratories. Using a system of pattern recognition, xRapid-Malaria can diagnose malaria from thick blood slides at the touch of a button. The technology streamlines the diagnostic process by providing an accessible solution for health workers. Malaria is a deadly global health problem, xRapid-Malaria gives much more people the means to test and treat the disease.

xRapid is currently working on xRapid-Lab, a natural extension of their initial app to characterise the culture of Plasmodium. This automated counter for malaria culture supports all researchers working on lab culture of Plasmodium species by offering a new tool to count parasites and red blood cells faster. 

Story:
xRapid is a Medtech company based primarily in London, UK with offices in Jakarta, Indonesia and San Francisco, USA. xRapid saw its beginnings in a laboratory in Jakarta. Our CTO, Professor David Mendels, recognised that he was able to develop a mobile solution for malaria diagnosis after attending a conference. Since then he has created xRapid; a powerful automated test that can be deployed anywhere in the field and has the potential to spot other diseases from tuberculosis to gonorrhoea.

Fortuna Fix is a next-generation regenerative medicine company focused on neuronal repair and regeneration. Our goal is to establish regenerative medicine as a new paradigm of healthcare, bringing real solutions to conditions that cannot be cured by current therapeutic modalities. We are the first in the field of Regenerative Medicine to have developed ethical regenerative medicine solutions that can truly restore functionality in patients following neurotrauma and neurodegeneration.
Our patented technology portfolio includes autologous neural precursor cells produced by direct reprogramming (drNPCTM) and regenerative implants Regeneration MatrixTM (RMxTM) and fully Automated Manufacturing of the drNPCTM (patent pending) for rapid scale-up and production of the drNPCTM.

Name: AAB Therapeutics
Description:
AAB Therapeutics develops precision biological drugs to treat cancer and autoimmune diseases without the systemic side-effects of chemotherapy. We are establishing a genetically programmable precision drug delivery platform that produces engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs). These nano-vesicles are decorated with antibodies to target them to specific cells and loaded with RNA drugs that kill the cancer cells. We use a proprietary AI model to choose the optimal combination of targeting antibodies. This modular platform can be rapidly re-targeted to other diseases by changing only a few components. Our initial focus is on liver and pancreatic cancer and autoimmunity, areas with significant unmet clinical need.

Registered in England and Wales as AAB Research Ltd.

Cardiaza is the first and only treatment that harnesses DNA methylation to address multiple underlying causes of symptomatic HCM, including established fibrosis, a key driver of disease progression.

Our mission is to address the longstanding challenges in the field of urine-based liquid biopsy, with a particular focus on sample preservation and accuracy of diagnosis.

Our innovative urine cell filtration device offers a breakthrough solution for rapid processing and preservation of urine samples, enabling precise and reliable diagnostic results. This advanced technology is designed to detect and monitor various urological conditions, including bladder cancer, endometrial cancer, urinary tract cancer, and prostate cancer.

At UGenDx, we are committed to advancing healthcare by providing accessible, non-invasive diagnostic tools that can improve early detection and treatment outcomes. With a focus on innovation and patient care, we are transforming the future of diagnostics.

Name: Sporette
Description:
Sporette is a social biotechnology venture developing ecological solutions to fungal disease, helping farmers protect harvests while restoring balance to the soil microbiome.

Our platform harnesses native soil microbes to restructure microbial ecosystems, creating a natural and scalable defence system that suppresses crop pathogens without chemicals, GMOs, or introduced species. Fungal disease currently causes 20-40% losses across major crops worldwide, making it one of the greatest constraints on agricultural productivity. 

Built on more than a decade of research, Sporette can be rapidly customised for specific crops and regions, with field trials starting in 3-6 months and measurable reductions in disease within the first year. 

As a social venture, our mission is to deliver scalable solutions that protect harvests and ultimately return the benefits of this technology to empower farmers and agricultural communities worldwide.

Name: ScionxBio
Description:
ScionxBio uses its xRNA platform to engineer long-acting RNA medicines that combine multiple therapies in a single treatment, with an initial focus on cardiometabolic disease. By expanding RNA beyond nature's four-letter alphabet, xRNA uses position-specific chemical modifications to sustain protein expression for weeks to months rather than days, while lowering innate immune sensing for a cleaner safety profile.
At the heart of the platform is the TERÅ engine, a closed-loop system in which deep-learning design, proprietary combinatorial assembly, high-throughput screening, and continuous model retraining work together to optimise each molecule for its specific payload. Because the hardest chronic diseases rarely stem from a single cause, xRNA is built to deliver programmable combinations of payloads aimed at multiple independent disease drivers in a coordinated, finely tuned way.
Our initial focus is cardiometabolic disease — one of medicine's largest and fastest-growing areas — and the same long-acting, multi-pathway approach extends to other complex chronic conditions, turning transient treatments into durable therapies for chronic disease. A spinoff from Eleven Therapeutics, ScionxBio operates across Cambridge (UK), Tel Aviv, and Cambridge (MA).

Name: Galytx
Description:
Galytx is a biotech company that develops galectin-3 targeted novel therapeutics.
Galectin-3 is a molecular target of exceptional clinical relevance in cancer, fibrosis and inflammation. Over expression of galectin-3 is an important driver of morbidity and morality associated with these diseases. Galytx is developing a unique portfolio of first in class, non-carbohydrate, wholly synthetic small molecule assets that target galectin-3 to address the  significant unmet clinical need in these disease areas.



Our pipeline includes both clinical and pre-clinical assets. Our lead clinical asset is a repurposed drug that has a strong and well-established safety record in chronic oral use, that enables a fast-track clinical development pathway. Our pre-clinical assets will be developed to produce high potency injectable therapeutics for acute use. Our lead disease indications are triple negative breast cancer and chronic heart failure, with our future vision to extend to address the full spectrum of galectin-3-mediated pathologies

Description:
Engineering Biology is a transformative technology that applies engineering concepts to design, build and manufacture cells and products.

Both the UK and South Korea are world leaders in engineering and synthetic biology, partly resulting from government funded initiatives to advance technology through supporting academic research and industrial hubs. A key area of publicly funded R&D infrastructure, and the focus of this partnership, are biofoundries: fully integrated facilities to enable rapid cell factory design, construction, and testing of biological systems.

Name: Parkure
Description:
Parkure is a Scottish company with the mission of finding a cure for Parkinson’s disease. Our highly qualified scientific and business team are committed to translating current scientific knowledge into treatments that stop the brain degeneration process of Parkinson’s disease.

Parkure has been founded to try to solve a problem. The problem is that, despite many scientific advances, there is still no sign of a cure for Parkinson’s disease. What do we mean by a cure? A cure is a treatment that stops the nerve cell degeneration process in its tracks.

Why is there this problem? The biology of Parkinson’s disease is complex, so that the well-established protein target-based drug development approaches used by industry have not worked so far.
Parkure is taking a different approach – to use a brain affected by Parkinson’s disease to test treatments.
Parkure is unique as a company in both its commitment to finding a cure for Parkinson’s disease and the way we are going about it.

Name: FUTURE HUMANITY VENTURES
Description:
Future Humanity Ventures is a team of dedicated engineers who share backgrounds in F1 motorsport and materials science. Our vision is simple – to revolutionise and lead the way in the collaborative development of ethical and sustainable technology. 
 
By bringing to bear our unique set of problem-solving skills, and a shared belief in creating a more sustainable and secure future for humanity, we are committed to driving innovation to its very limits to provide a greener and safer future for all.
 
We act as catalysts for the development and implementation of innovative solutions that will transform industries and empower people around the globe. By harnessing the agile methods and expertise that have made UK motorsport a global leader in advanced composites, we can facilitate the re-engineering of the material properties of any product. Our innovations reduce CO2 footprint, enhance safety, and improve performance – thereby promoting and proving, along the way, that the development of sustainable technology is the only way forward.
 
We are on a journey – driven to prioritise sustainability, to embrace innovation, and to celebrate the power of collaboration. Every day is hard work, but every day brings reward, and every day takes us a step closer to a more sustainable and cleaner planet.

Name: GlycoWeb
Description:
Led by the University of Nottingham, GlycoWeb is driven by an experienced, innovative, and multidisciplinary team of researchers from five top UK institutions with key overseas collaborators.    
Our team comprises experts in various fields including the development and application of advanced 3D models called gastruloids, structural analysis of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), and transcriptional regulation of glycan biosynthesis. 
Together, we are committed to advancing the understanding and application of GAGs in biomedical sciences. 
We perform integrative analyses of transcriptomics, proteomics, and detailed GAG structural and spatial analyses using an advanced 3D stem cell development model (gastuloids) as an exemplar model system. This enables us to build, test and refine our understanding of GAG biosynthesis and degradation using novel GAG-binding probes and analysis techniques, in a dynamic system. 
Our work will make GAG research accessible to the broader scientific community and facilitate the development of new therapies and biotechnological applications. Impact will reach across fields such as mammalian development, regenerative medicine, and medical research (e.g. cancer, diabetes, kidney failure and genetic disorders). 
Our mission is to transform the practical biomedical understanding of glycosaminoglycans into a comprehensive web of predictable processes.    
We strive to: 

Break down current barriers limiting the application of GAGs in biological sciences and biotechnological fields. 
Empower the development of novel treatments for diseases via the application of innovative biotechnological tools created by our advanced platform. 
Democratise GAG research through training and by the development of new, accessible methods. 

Through these efforts, we aim to create new opportunities for commercial and societal benefits, ultimately improving health outcomes and fostering innovation in glycobiology and related disciplines.

Optima’s “vehicle” particles can transport any drug to any tissue with safety and precision, while improving penetration and delivery to the hardest tissue of the body, the blood brain barrier (BBB), by 80% (unprecedented).

Leading to decreasing toxicity, no need of higher dosages, enhancement of drug performance, & better patient outcomes.

Name: Latus Therapeutics
Description:
Latus Therapeutics Limited, founded in 2019, is a leading research and experimental development biotech company with a vision to find a cure for cancer. We are specifically looking at the B-cell Lymphomas in order to get a better understanding of the underlying signalling mechanism of the cell and its potential in helping people to combat cancer.

Today, in response to the public health crisis, Latus Therapeutics has refocused its efforts to originate not for profit initiative to find a treatment for the patients tested positive with the COVID-19. More information about the trials can be found on our website. Latus' team is contributing their time for free.

Name: NovaHealZ

Born out of the University of Glasgow, NovaHealZ combines scientific research with practical innovation to create solutions that improve healing outcomes and patient care.

Our flagship innovation focuses on biocompatible hydrogel-based wound dressings designed to support the treatment of diabetic foot ulcers, post-surgical wounds, and maternal recovery following C-sections. By leveraging advanced biomaterials and skin-compatible technologies, we aim to enhance healing, reduce complications, and improve quality of life for patients.

Beyond advanced wound care, NovaHealZ is building a hydrogel innovation platform that extends into skin health and biomaterial-based solutions, bridging research, product development, and translational healthcare innovation.

NovaHealZ was recognized as the winner of the FemTech Hackathon, supported by the EIBF Prize 2025 and the Converge Microfinance Grant, and selected as a Finalist in the Converge KickStart Challenge 2025.

With its roots in Scotland and expanding innovation and R&D activities internationally, NovaHealZ is committed to redefining wound care and skin health through science-backed, sustainable, and patient-centered design.

By bringing together biology, renewable energy and advanced engineering, we seek to create a new kind of food-production system that is both sustainable and independent of agricultural land.

Our long-term mission is to make nutritious food accessible anywhere, even in places where farming is difficult or impossible. We focus particularly on cancer vaccines. By developing advanced computational models, we improve the prediction of tumour antigens that are most likely to be recognised by the immune system. This enables the design of both personalised neoantigen vaccines and scalable off-the-shelf strategies, supporting prevention, early intervention, and treatment. Our AI platforms work alongside robotic and automated laboratory systems, accelerating discovery while maintaining biological rigour.

A BBSRC-funded network that promotes collaborations between industry and academia.

This Durham, Kent and Manchester Universities-led network is one of six phase II BBSRC NIBB, announced in November 2018.

The Network brings together scientific communities working on metals in biology to accelerate research relevant to industrial biotechnology and bioenergy. Almost a half of the reactions of life are catalysed by metals. This means that a large proportion of bio-industries depend directly, or indirectly, on the catalytic activities of metals in proteins. Academic members work with biomanufacturing and bioenergy sectors to enhance metalloenzyme activities to generate new products and increase the profitability and sustainability of existing products. Name: TamRx Systems
Description:
TamRx Systems builds a therapy-aware, clinical-trial simulation layer for medical AI.

Today’s medical AI systems largely stop at pattern detection in clinical data. They rarely model how interventions behave under real therapeutic conditions or how drug mechanisms translate into observable outputs across clinical monitoring systems.

TamRx Systems addresses this gap by simulating drug–system interactions in a clinical-trial-like framework, mapping pharmacological actions to their effects on physiological signals and medical device readouts.

This enables a structured view of how treatments propagate through biological systems and how those effects are captured in real-world diagnostics and monitoring technologies.

Founded by Mounsif Tamani, PharmD, with training in biomedical data science and pharmacology, TamRx Systems operates at the intersection of computational pharmacology, clinical reasoning, and AI system design.

Our goal is to move medical AI from passive prediction toward therapeutically grounded, trial-like reasoning of interventions and outcomes.

New treatment and healthcare improvements over the last fifty years have helped save and extend lives. Consequently, we now have an increasing ageing population that suffer with multimorbidity and healthcare systems across the world are under pressure to cope.

Solutions to address this issue have the potential to simultaneously deliver substantial economic improvement for global health services whilst providing more benefits to humanity than at any other time in our history.

We have a unique understanding of how stem cells can be manipulated to produce optimised stem cell secretions, we call Secretomix and are exploring the effects of our products on various disease states, with the target of extending the period of living healthily.

The Secretomix platform is designed to create various secretome formulations for different diseases. It is anticipated to produce new therapeutics delivering novel regenerative approaches, which are scalable and are expected to have applications across a wide range of diseases.

Name: PharmaKure Limited
Description:
Over 50 milllion people worldwide are living with Alzheimer's disease. This is expected to increase to over 150 million by 2050. The associated health and social costs are expected to reach £1.5 trillion globally by 2030. 

While hundreds of drugs have been tested over the past decades, no cure has yet been found. 

PharmaKure have developed a unique screening approach to identify existing approved drugs which show activity as amyloid disaggregators. The misfolding of amyloid proteins in the brain is hypothesised to be a cause of Alzheimer's, with the oligomer forms being particularly toxic, so a disaggregating drug shows real promise as a therapeutic. 

This screening platform has identified two drugs showing significant activity in combination. These have been patented as repurposed drugs for Alzheimer's Disease, and are ready for Phase II clinical trials.

Furthermore, our diagnostics partners have developed a unique method for the detection of Alzheimer's biomarkers.  This allows for selection of a precise subject group in trials, in addition to providing a method for monitoring the trial, using whole blood samples.

RYPEN technology is either coated onto or embedded into packaging materials to create active fresh‐produce packaging that selectively adsorbs ethylene— the natural plant hormone responsible for ripening—drawing these molecules from the air into its molecular structure and locking them within. 

By moderating ethylene in this way, RYPEN protects nearby fresh produce, slowing premature or excessive ripening while still enabling it to ripen naturally, reach and maintain its peak flavour window, and extend its overall postharvest longevity. 

Developed to selectively target ethylene molecules, RYPEN moderates exposure levels efficiently over long periods. This precise mode of action sets RYPEN apart within the ethylene‐control market: fresh produce protected with RYPEN is not subjected to chemical oxidation processes, nor does it rely on biochemical alteration of the fruit. As a result, RYPEN‐protected produce remains safe, lasts longer, and retains fully natural ripening behaviour and flavour development. 

All RYPEN products are approved for food contact under EU and US FDA regulations, ensuring they can be used safely and effectively in close proximity to fresh produce.

Description:
Orexia is developing orexin receptor agonists for the treatment of narcolepsy, a rare neurological condition that affects the brain's ability to regulate the normal sleep-wake cycle

We aspire to develop innovative medicines that address the full spectrum of orexin dysfunction in disease areas where there is high unmet clinical need. Orexia is designing novel oral small molecule OX2R agonists and positive modulators, which would influence orexin neurotransmission differently. 
Orexin agonists and positive modulators have the potential to treat a wide range of disorders which are inadequately treated today, most notably Narcolepsy Type 1 (NT1) which is caused by profound loss of orexin-producing neurons. NT1 is a chronic rare disease that usually starts during adolescence and is estimated to effect over 3 million people worldwide. Orexin agonists and positive modulators will directly address the underlying disease pathology of NT1, and may have the potential for greater efficacy and tolerability than current therapies.

We aim to provide customers with the vital information they need to make fast, early decisions about compound progression in drug discovery to save money and time. Our mitochondrial screening is undertaken in patient-derived cells, enabling assessment of compound activity and efficacy for many complex diseases such as neurodegeneration, cancer and diabetes. We use state-of-the-art techniques, developed by Professor Heather Mortiboys over the last decade, to measure numerous mitochondrial characteristics. This includes, but is not limited to,  function, morphology, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial DNA, mitophagy and the interaction of mitochondria with other organelles. This vast amount of data, collected in high throughput screens, can be condensed into a single score of mitochondrial health enabling rapid interpretation of the data and early termination of ineffective compounds. It also provides a solid platform for further target validation and mechanism of action studies for effective compounds. All of our screens, from early to late preclinical discovery, are conducted in patient-derived cells to best replicate complex diseases and ensure the greatest confidence in translation to successful trials in the clinic.

Name: Protostem-AI
Description:
Stem cell research has a big problem, and we're here to solve it. Currently, the stem cell technologies market value stands at $14bn with a global input of $2.2bn in 2024 alone. So why are there only 30 approved stem cell derived therapies globally? Why, also, are none of these 30 derived from embryonic or induced pluripotent stem cell start points?

The answer is waste. Waste which comes from a lack of standardisation across stem cell research and manufacturing. Waste which results in 70% of stem cell research lacking reproducibility or a tangible output. Waste which means 99.8% of stem cell therapeutic clinical trials will fail. Current stem cell project management methodologies are poorly equipped to offset this waste. There are no gold standard processes for stem cell research and manufacturing in the academic and commercial sector. Similarly, current troubleshooting and optimisation processes are logistically demanding and reliant on long end to end development cycles. Failed processes therefore extend beyond acceptable parameters and yet the sector lacks the tools to implement change.

We are a team of stem cell biologists and AI experts who decided make this change. We present Protostem-AI, the world's first end to end project management tool tailored to stem cell research and manufacturing. Our application allows multiple users to design and monitor stem cell projects. Using agentic AI and federated learning models Protostem-AI can spot developing problems in real time, suggesting process additions and changes to guarantee successful outcomes. Protostem-AI can suggest equipment available to hand, monitor consumable stock levels and implement ordering when needed. Finally, the application can collate research outputs into bespoke formats, from in house reports to publications and patent applications. 

If you would like to learn more please visit our website or contact our CEO at Dominic@protostem-ai.com.

Name: UCL iGEM 2018
Description:
International Genetically Engineered Machines (iGEM) is an international science, engineering art, design, mathematics and public engagement competition. 

iGEM is organised by the iGEM Foundation which was part of MIT until 2012 when it formed a not-for-profit spinout company which is still based near to MIT.  The organisation has grown every year since 2004 and there are now many 'flavours' of iGEM including iGEM-Entrepreneurship, iGEM Community Labs and iGEM-High School.

The iGEM Foundation fosters scientific research and education through organising and operating the iGEM Competition, the premier student synthetic biology competition. The foundation fosters scientific research and education by establishing and operating the Registry of Standard Biological Parts, a community collection of biological components. iGEM also promotes the advancement of science and education by developing an open community of students and practitioners in schools, laboratories, research institutes, and industry. iGEM has a long history of involving students and the public in the development of the new field of synthetic biology.

We are the UCL iGEM for 2018. This year we are working on the chimeric spider silk. We are expanding its applications in tissue regeneration and metal extraction. Our goal is to customise a natural material that is stronger than teflon but softer than a cloud.

We are dedicated to restoring hope and intimacy for millions affected by sexual health challenges. Name: Unblinded Neuro
Description:
Competitive analysis in neuroscience mostly restates what sponsors say about themselves.

I build market maps that do the opposite: regulator labels, registry entries, patents, filings and papers, read against each other. Trade press and commercial databases are good for finding out that something exists and not much else, so every lead is followed through to the document behind it before it goes into a file.

Two habits, neither of them clever.

Every mechanism claim carries a confidence tier. HIGH means a primary document exists. MEDIUM means it is an inference, and says so. LOW means secondary coverage only. Low-confidence rows stay in the file marked rather than quietly disappearing, because how much of a field is resting on nothing is usually worth knowing.

Human data never shares a table with mouse or monkey data. Sponsors blur those two constantly and it is normally where the interesting part is hiding.

The most recent map covers non-invasive delivery across the blood-brain barrier: 47 in-scope programmes, seven delivery classes, 71 registry records. Two products in that field hold approvals that survive a check against a regulator record. Both treat the same lysosomal disease and neither treats a neurodegenerative one, which is worth knowing before anyone takes "clinically validated delivery" at face value.

You get the deck and the research behind it. One row per programme, a source log with a retrievable identifier for every claim, and a file listing everything I could not verify and why. I would read that last file first.

The person doing the research is the person you talk to. No account team, no associate drafting it.

Background: scientific due diligence and market analysis at Beechbrook Capital. Before that, Senior Scientist at Neuro-Bio Ltd, a neurodegeneration research company, carrying out research at the forefront of the Alzheimer's biomarker field.

Listeners can expect to learn cool facts and get a general background for everything related to the episode's journal article through a visually immersive 'journal club' approach to the podcast, Ft. narratives and first-person perspectives from the authors/scientists themselves. It's a fine line to manage, but we're doing our best! And the more feedback from people from all levels of background/understanding, the better!

Name: GeneAId
Description:
Every year, millions of genetic variants are identified through clinical sequencing — and for patients across the Arab world and Gulf region, the tools used to interpret them were never built with their populations in mind.

Around 86% of individuals in global genomic databases are of European ancestry. For the 400+ million people across MENA, this means higher rates of misclassification, diagnostic uncertainty, and AI models that systematically underserve them. This is the gap GeneAId was founded to close.

GeneAId is a clinical AI startup building an explainable, ACMG-aligned machine learning framework for genetic variant classification — trained on 2.95 million curated ClinVar submissions and designed with Arab and Gulf ancestry equity as a core principle. The pipeline classifies variants across four clinically actionable ACMG categories, achieving a macro ROC-AUC of 0.86, with human-in-the-loop interpretability at its core. Unlike black-box genomic tools, GeneAId explains its predictions — clinicians see not just what the model predicts, but why.

GeneAId is built for real-world clinical deployment — fully reproducible, designed for app integration, and structured around the governance and auditability standards clinical environments demand. We are not building another research prototype. We are building infrastructure for a region that has been waiting for it.

Founded by Lara Masad (Co-Founder, Chief AI Officer & CEO) and Dr. Lina Al-Shobaki (Co-Founder & Clinical Lead), GeneAId brings together the technical depth and clinical expertise needed to build tools that work for the populations global genomics has historically ignored.

We are open to clinical partnerships, research collaborations, accelerator programmes, and investor conversations.

Name: MORPHOGEN-IX LIMITED
Description:
MORPHOGEN-IX Limited is a drug discovery company founded in 2015 by Index Ventures to develop bone morphogenetic proteins as a novel therapy for the treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension

Pulmonary arterial hypertension is a severe and life-limiting disease that affects the blood vessels in the lungs, leading to heart failure, and leaves sufferers feeling breathless and exhausted. Current treatments mainly target symptoms and the prognosis remains poor. The only effective cure is transplantation of the lungs or heart and lungs, which has associated risks and complications.

Compromised bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) receptor type II (BMPR-II) signalling in endothelial cells plays a pivotal role in the pathobiology PAH, as identified from human genetic studies.

BMP9 and 10 represent circulating ligands that selectively bind and activate BMPR-II receptor complexes on endothelial cells. Administration of exogenous BMP9 has been shown to augment endothelial BMPR-II signalling and reverse PAH in several rodent models of disease.

Our goal is to explore the potential of BMP9 and BMP10 as potential therapies for PAH.

The company follows the semi-virtual model with a hub based in Cambridge, UK. The company founders are experts in the field of PAH and BMPs. The team is staffed with experienced drug discovery professionals to direct an out-sourced development program. This model ensures maximum capital efficiency without sacrificing quality.

Description:

The programme is supported by extensive pre-clinical work to demonstrate the complementary nature of ultrasound and visual imaging, along with studies of multimodal diagnosis and therapy as the SONOPILL  travels through the GI tract.  This is opening up both challenges and opportunities in areas including ultrasound device and systems design, microengineering and microelectronic packaging, sensor suites for diagnosis and intervention, and routes to translation into clinical practice.

Our programme's carefully structured but open-ended approach maximises the possibility to meet these challenges while delivering international leading science and engineering in multimodality capsule endoscopy. The ultimate aim is to provide greater capabilities for the clinician, more acceptable practice for the patient population, and lower costs for economic wellbeing.

Multiple Safe Surface Sensors are simply placed around any public area where the transmission of viruses such as COVID may occur prior to the sanitation process. The sensors can be placed on both hard and soft surfaces.

XSTREAM employs a proprietary system to convert H2O through its reactor core into powerful Cluster Ions to continually destroy the bugs on contact.  XStream Infection Control is the ONLY system that works 24/7/365, is not hazardous to human health and does not use chemicals or lethal gases.  
Under the direction of Kelly Reynolds, PhD. a scientific testing protocol was developed over 3 years and published for the University of Arizona.  The results:
97.61% reduction of airborne bacteria and viruses over six hours.
99.9% reduction of surface bacteria, viruses and b. thurgingiensis (C-diff surrogate) over 6 hours
99.8% reduction of bacteria and viruses on fabric/fomites surfaces.
Environment 99.9% clean in 24-48 hours and continually thereafter .

'Bringing the cell therapy, gene therapy and regenerative medicine community together for the benefit of all’

The London Regenerative Medicine Network (LRMN) is the largest and most successful cell therapy, gene therapy and regenerative medicine network in the UK if not globally. Founded in 2005, the LRMN remains an independent ‘not for profit’ organization firmly embedded in the community. This grass-roots network is free for all to join and prides itself on its inclusivity. The LRMN holds regular monthly meetings, which are free to attend, and focused on the entire spectrum of cell and gene therapy and regenerative medicine, but always with a commitment to translation. By 2015, approximately 300 international speakers had presented to over 25,000 participants. The LRMN has enabled countless introductions, facilitated numerous collaborations and the launch of the journal, "Regenerative Medicine". Through its extensive networking activities, the LRMN is totally focused on accelerating the attainment of one common goal: the delivery of safe, efficacious cell and gene therapies that can be affordably manufactured at scale for use in routine clinical practice.

Description:
Groundwork Health was founded with the patient voice in mind, our vision is to enable equitable health outcomes for those whose voices have gone unheard for too long.

Clinical research is notoriously lacking in representing people from diverse backgrounds. This has a dangerous downstream effect on underrepresented populations, whose genetics could massively influence their reaction to a particular medicine. It also means that for diseases which disproportionately affect people of a specific racial background, will not have effective drugs developed to treat them. 

Our diverse, passionate team of industry experts engage with communities directly to address the stereotypes associated with clinical trials, a big part of which is inviting, listening, building from their experiences and ideas, as well as engaging with caregivers and HCPs.
